headline: Certificate Transparency SCT signature verification now functions (it previously rejected every SCT); broader Redis-client and TLS-verification test coverage
summary: The Certificate Transparency SCT verifier read the wrong field for its log-key algorithm cross-check, so every SCT failed that gate before the signature was ever checked — verifyScts could never return a verified result and requireScts rejected every certificate. It now reads the correct field and functions. Alongside the fix, error and edge branches of b.redisClient and b.network.tls come under explicit test.

items.title: Certificate Transparency SCT signature verification now works instead of rejecting every SCT
items.body: b.network.tls.ct.verifyScts cross-checks each SCT's signature algorithm against the registered log key's type (RFC 6962 §2.1.4) before verifying the signature. That check read the SCT's algorithm from a field name the parser does not emit, so the value was always undefined, the algorithm gate always failed with log-key-algo-mismatch, and the actual signature verification was never reached — verifyScts could never report a verified SCT, and b.network.tls.ct.requireScts consequently rejected every certificate. The gate now reads the parsed sigAlgo field, so a matching log key reaches signature verification and a genuine algorithm mismatch is still refused. The prior behaviour failed closed (it rejected rather than accepted), so no invalid certificate was ever trusted; operators who had enabled SCT enforcement will now see valid SCTs verify.

items.title: Error- and edge-path tests for the Redis client and TLS-verification primitives
items.body: b.redisClient (RESP framing and protocol-error edges, split replies, AUTH / SELECT on connect, push-message demux, connect/command timeouts, socket-error and close teardown) and b.network.tls (OCSP and Certificate-Transparency parse and verification branches, ECH config framing, and PKIX host/SAN matching) now have explicit tests for their boundary branches, driven through local fake servers and crafted certificates.
